title: Desk design v1: the Claude desk DRIVES the trading (finds/enters, manages, exits trades) and is the teacher the system's MLs learn from; entry generation is its entry stage
note: Filed 2026-10-26 ~06:45Z by the manager from the operator's popup answer on DESK-DESIGN Q2 (quoted verbatim on DESK-DESIGN): the desk should generate entries by monitoring live markets, more than vetoing strategy entries. Scope of this row: (a) amend docs/plans/claude-trading-desk-DESIGN.md -- § 2.3 market-watch enum gains a propose_entry intent (symbol, side, entry/stop/TP with a REAL predictive TP per the TP doctrine, thesis, confidence, info_cutoff), § 2.3 'never' line reworded, packet/decision schemas, grading per DESK-9; (b) the D-S0 test design: pre-registered blind replay of generated entries vs the strategy baseline, net of the full cost stack, as research/queue units; (c) the ladder: shadow-recorded -> paper (bybit_1/alpaca_paper soak, mechanical 1-2 trades) -> real money only under a new operator-granted mandate after D-S0 passes. Design + test design only; no order path. Depends on DESK-0 schema (landed). [2026-10-26 06:52Z manager] OPERATOR 2026-10-26 ~06:50Z, verbatim: "just to be clear about the entry stage of the desk project, like, the goal isn't for Claude to be reviewing the entries. That's, I mean, we can have that also, that's nice, but when I say the trading desk does entries, I mean that they find trades that the system isn't finding. So, like, I don't even know what that restriction on should Claude be able to deny an entry, like, where that even came from. That's just, like, not the design at all. Completely wrong direction." Scope clarified: this is THE entry stage of the desk, not an add-on to entry review. Rewrite design § 0/§ 2.1/§ 2.3/§ 8/§ 10/§ 11: market watch + entry role propose new trades (symbol, side, entry/stop/real predictive TP, thesis, confidence, info_cutoff) the system is not taking; remove the 'never a new entry' clause and the veto framing (entry review of strategy packages becomes optional, record-only); drop Q2 and the MD-DESK-SKIP proposal; DESK-7 replay covers generated entries vs a no-trade / strategy baseline net of the full cost stack; ladder: recorded -> paper soak (mechanical 1-2 trades) -> real money under an operator-granted mandate. [2026-10-26 06:56Z manager] WIDENED to the full design v1 rewrite. OPERATOR VISION 2026-10-26 ~06:55Z, verbatim: "the whole idea here with the trading desk is that we're trying to build a system where Claude isn't just weighing in on the system's trades. Claude is, the Claude trading desk is driving the trading, and the MLs, the systems MLs that we're building are learning from that Claude decision-making how to do it themselves so that we can eventually remove Claude from the flow and have only our own AIs doing the trading. But the whole point is to have Claude pushing the whole trading operation so that we can use that as the basis for teaching the MLs." Scope: rewrite docs/plans/claude-trading-desk-DESIGN.md end to end around 'Claude drives, MLs learn': (1) roles: market watch + entry generation (new trades the strategies are not taking), in-trade management (= live trade review, already live in apply), exit; strategy-entry review optional; (2) every desk decision is a teacher label with packet + outcome, feeding CJ-2/DESK-11 and the distillation design (docs/plans/ml-claude-distillation-DESIGN.md), with a stated hand-off path from Claude to the system's own models (student shadow -> student advisory -> student drives, per role, on measured agreement/net R); (3) safety stays: per-account RiskManager, ladder (D-S0 blind replay net of full cost stack -> paper soak 1-2 mechanical trades -> real money under operator-granted mandates), no halting, per-trade refusals; (4) re-sequence §10 rows DESK-0..DESK-14 to that goal and list any new rows; (5) open questions only where no data settles them. Design doc + row edits only; no order path. [2026-10-26 06:58Z manager] OPERATOR, verbatim: "we should start with the live review. It just needs to, like, the restrictions and the design doc shouldn't be based around keeping it at that level. It should be based around moving towards the full-fledged cloud trading desk, which again is the basis for training our MLs, which means that the design doc also needs to ensure that we're using the desk in the correct way in order to generate data that trains the models and not just executing the trades and then forgetting about them." Relayed to the lane (trigger trig_018NbbJFsFN8RMxbRDkmkpV8): live review = phase 1 of the desk; every restriction written as a stage with its lift condition; new first-class section 'The desk as a training-data generator' (point-in-time packets, decisions incl. no-action, priced alternatives, verdicts/fills, outcomes joined back, stable ids, canonical store, label quality, coverage/exploration, and a 'recorded but never trained on' detector). [2026-10-26 07:02Z manager] OPERATOR, verbatim: "we can pace ourselves. I don't want us to go over the budgets here, but I want to make sure that ... the second half of this is once the desk is up and running and the data flow to the MLs is set up correctly ... that pipeline is working, and that ... all the infrastructure is there for them to actually learn and grow based on this pipeline, so that ... it's not like we end up having this great trading desk that is pushing structured data into a void ... we can have the trading desk and measure the trading desk, and that we can measure the MLs and measure how much they're improving and measure them against the cloud trading desk, so that we have ... a benchmark ... even if we're not necessarily building everything end-to-end right now or even this week, that we have the plan so that we know what we're working against as things develop." Relayed (trig_014ek4pTdeQRJ2hSfzheXWca): v1 adds 'The second half' -- pipeline health (desk record -> dataset -> training -> registry, liveness per hop, never-trained-on detector), one scorecard (desk per role; each student on the same decisions; student-vs-desk benchmark + improvement curve OOS; hand-off and demotion thresholds), reporting homes, and later-phase rows. Written as a PLAN within the $12 ceiling (budget pacing).
